channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Turkey's diplomatic tensions escalate over religious attire dispute
item.description: Tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey have intensified following a dispute over religious attire in Azerbaijani schools. Turkish criticism of a dress code revision banning hijabs was met with counter-criticism from Azerbaijani state media. Azerbaijan has also sought international arrest warrants for journalists in Turkey, accusing them of inciting unrest.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan reduces real estate transaction fees; money transfers and trade data released
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has significantly reduced state duties for real estate transactions. August saw a decrease in money transfers to Kyrgyzstan, primarily from Russia. Russia regained its position as the top importer of chocolate and confectionery. Switzerland expressed readiness to expand cooperation in hydropower and disaster prevention.

item.title: Kazakh citizens returning from Russia after military conscription; school curriculum and military service changes discussed
item.description: Kazakh citizens who went to Russia for work and were conscripted into the military are returning home. Discussions are underway regarding the promotion of the USSR in an Almaty school and potential changes to military service obligations following a Caspian Sea tragedy.

item.title: Illegal meat processing workshop discovered in Astana during livestock theft operation
item.description: An illegal meat processing workshop was discovered in Astana as part of a national operation targeting livestock theft. The facility processed meat products without necessary permits or veterinary-sanitary conclusions, according to the Veterinary Control and Supervision Committee. Violators face administrative fines.

item.title: Uzbek Man Accused of Stealing $12 Million in Cargo in the US
item.description: An Uzbek man is accused in the United States of stealing approximately $12 million worth of cargo. The suspect allegedly operated using several false names and altered identification documents. He and his accomplices are accused of stealing a total of 24 large shipments, though the suspect denies the charges.

item.title: Exhibition on UN Cooperation Opens at National Museum of Kazakhstan
item.description: An exhibition titled 'GLOCAL: Global Goals. Local Lives' has opened at the National Museum of Kazakhstan, celebrating UN Day. The exhibition showcases 30 stories illustrating practical results of Kazakhstan's cooperation with UN agencies across five areas of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. First Deputy Foreign Minister Yerzhan Ashikbayev attended the opening.

item.title: Energy Company Workers Rescued After Getting Stuck in Snow in East Kazakhstan
item.description: Seven energy company employees became stranded in a snowdrift in two vehicles while working on power lines in the East Kazakhstan region. Rescuers used off-road vehicles to evacuate the workers to the nearest settlement. The employees did not require medical attention. Drivers are urged to monitor weather warnings.

item.title: Uzbekistan Fines Cement Producer for Failing to Meet Delivery Obligations
item.description: Uzbekistan's competition committee has fined "Ahgangarancement" for failing to deliver cement on time. The decision followed complaints from two companies that had contracts with the producer but did not receive their orders. The company also failed to fully meet obligations from exchange trades, violating competition law.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Outlines Ambitious Development Goals Through 2030
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has set Kyrgyzstan's development goals up to 2030, emphasizing a holistic approach. He stressed the importance of integrating economic projects with public administration quality, specialist training, and family well-being, highlighting the interconnectedness of all processes for effective implementation.

item.title: Switzerland and UN WFP Provide 5,000 Food Packages to Kyrgyzstan's Emergency Ministry
item.description: Switzerland and the UN World Food Programme have donated 5,000 food packages to Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations. Each package is designed to feed one person for 10 days during emergencies. The supplies, made from local products, will aid disaster victims, especially in remote areas.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov Inspects Shymkent's Industrial Zones and Road Infrastructure
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited Shymkent to review its socio-economic development and the implementation of presidential directives on economic growth and road quality. He inspected the "Zhuldyz" and "Tassay" industrial zones and a road interchange, also reviewing public space improvements.

item.title: Two Tajik Migrants Rescued Locals from Fire in Russia's Bashkortostan
item.description: Two Tajik citizens, Khisravshoh Malikоv and Zohirshoh Hasanov, have been hailed as heroes in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan, Russia, for rescuing two local residents from a fire. The incident highlights the bravery of Tajik migrants in the face of danger.

item.title: New York Times: Pakistani military and intelligence officials met with Taliban opponents
item.description: According to the New York Times, Pakistani military and intelligence officials have met with armed opponents of the Taliban. The report details these meetings, suggesting a complex engagement by Pakistan in the Afghan conflict. Further details are expected as the situation evolves.

item.title: Russia Seeks Clarification on New Entry Rules for Kazakhstan
item.description: Russia has requested clarification from Kazakhstan regarding new entry regulations. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that detailed information about the QazETA system has been sent through diplomatic channels to all affected countries. This follows a request for clarification from Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes Saiga Antelope Horns Worth $180 Million in Smuggling Attempt
item.description: Kazakhstan's border guards have thwarted an attempt to illegally export saiga antelope horns valued at approximately $180 million. The seizure occurred on October 20 at the Khorgos international border cooperation center, where 620 horns were found destined for China. The case materials have been transferred to the competent authority for further proceedings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves National Program for Chess Development and Popularization
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree approving the National Program for the Development and Popularization of Chess in Kyrgyzstan for 2026-2030. The program aims to create conditions for chess development, mass participation, and enhance the competitiveness of Kyrgyz chess players internationally.

item.title: Kazakhstan Showcases Seven Years of Achievements on Festive Billboards
item.description: In anticipation of Republic Day, Kazakhstan is highlighting its achievements over the past seven years through festive billboards across the country. These displays focus on key indicators, particularly in the social sector, reflecting tangible changes experienced by citizens in education, healthcare, and support for families.

item.title: SCO Government Heads Convene 25th Meeting in Dushanbe
item.description: The 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states took place in Dushanbe, chaired by Tajikistan. Participants discussed global economic architecture transformation, strengthening SCO economic interaction, and implementing joint projects. Prime ministers and government representatives from SCO member states attended, along with SCO Secretary General Nurlan Ermekbayev.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Bangladesh Discuss Priorities for 81st UN General Assembly Session
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with the President of the 81st UN General Assembly session and Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Halilur Rahman. They exchanged views on UN cooperation, priorities for the upcoming session, and current international issues. Saidov thanked Rahman for supporting Uzbekistan's international initiatives.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received the President of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly. They exchanged views on international issues, including the development of regional cooperation in Central Asia. The meeting focused on fostering dialogue and strengthening partnerships within the OSCE framework.

item.title: Egypt Eases Entry for Kazakh Citizens Following Foreign Minister's Visit
item.description: Egypt has removed Kazakhstan from a list of countries with additional entry requirements for tourists. This decision, reached during talks between Kazakh Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi and his Egyptian counterpart, aims to simplify travel for Kazakh citizens and boost tourism exchanges. The two nations also discussed strengthening political, economic, and investment ties, and signed a protocol expanding visa-free travel for holders of official passports.

item.title: Tasks Set for Kashkadarya's Potential, Population Income Growth, and Job Creation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on the socioeconomic development of the Kashkadarya region. The president emphasized unlocking the region's potential, increasing incomes, and creating jobs, aiming to eradicate poverty and unemployment by year-end. Discussions focused on boosting value-added production, utilizing gas and mineral resources, and expanding petrochemical and chemical industries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Cabinet and UN WFP Discuss School Nutrition Program Development
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan met with the acting Executive Director of the UN World Food Programme (WFP) to discuss cooperation. Key topics included developing the school nutrition system, supporting vulnerable families, and enhancing targeted food assistance. Both sides expressed interest in continued collaboration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Ties with China and Germany in Energy-Efficient Housing
item.description: An international forum on energy-efficient housing construction, focusing on technologies and cooperation between China, Germany, and Kazakhstan, was held in Astana. Discussions centered on implementing modern energy-efficient technologies in Kazakhstan's housing sector, highlighting the potential for significant energy savings compared to current consumption.

item.title: Ex-KNB Officer Claims KGB Was Saving Hostages During January Events
item.description: A former KNB (National Security Committee) officer, Ruslan Isakov, claims in a cassation appeal to the Supreme Court that the KGB was actively involved in saving hostages during the January events. This is the third part of a series based on his appeal, which also disputes the narrative of '20,000 terrorists' and criticizes President Tokayev.

item.title: US and Israel Reportedly Planning New Strikes Against Iran After Midterm Elections
item.description: The United States and Israel are reportedly developing plans for new strikes against Iran, potentially commencing after the US midterm elections on November 3rd. The New York Times, citing sources, suggests a short but intense operation targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile arsenals. The goal is to exert economic pressure on Tehran. However, striking oil infrastructure might be avoided to prevent further fuel price hikes. The underground Pikaks nuclear facility is mentioned as a key target.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Track Oil Movement from Well to Gas Station by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to achieve 80% digital traceability of energy resources by 2028, according to the Ministry of Energy. This initiative involves creating a unified digital accounting system for oil and petroleum products from extraction to retail. The system is expected to improve data consistency, reduce resource losses, and enhance transparency in their circulation. Officials visited fuel retail sites and storage facilities to review current measurement and accounting systems.

item.title: Uzbekistan's ISRS Director Participates in Global Security Forum in Doha
item.description: Eldor Aripov, Director of the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies under the President of Uzbekistan (ISRS), attended the 8th Global Security Forum in Doha, Qatar, from October 19-21, 2026. The forum convened government officials, international organizations, experts, and media from over 100 countries to discuss the future of international alliances amid shifting global power dynamics.

item.title: Tajikistan Launches Measles and Rubella Vaccination Campaign for Young Children
item.description: Tajikistan is conducting a measles and rubella vaccination campaign for children aged 6 months to 5 years from October 26 to November 6, 2026. The campaign aims to immunize over 818,000 children, excluding areas where vaccinations were already administered in 2025. This initiative seeks to prevent the spread of these diseases.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Meets EEC Chairman to Discuss Trade Facilitation
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan met with the Chairman of the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC). Emphasis was placed on the importance of adopting a new cooperation plan aimed at reducing trade barriers and digitizing customs and transport procedures. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Tajikistan Parliament Approves New Territorial Defense Law
item.description: Tajikistan's parliament has adopted a new territorial defense law. Previously, important state territories and facilities were protected by internal Ministry of Defense documents. The implications of this new law are currently being detailed.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Strengthen Oversight of Charitable Boxes and Online Fundraisers
item.description: Kazakhstan proposes new regulations for collecting money through social media and the internet for personal needs. Individuals collecting funds will be required to report on how charitable donations are spent. The Ministry of Culture and Information has published the draft law.

item.title: Water and Soil Pollution Found at East Kazakhstan Mine Site
item.description: Environmental violations were discovered at the Novo-Berezovskoye deposit in East Kazakhstan. Following resident complaints, an inspection revealed that Dengbo Success Minerals LTD discharged mine water into the Berezovka River. Lab tests showed elevated pollutant levels. The company faces administrative penalties and has been ordered to rectify the issues.

item.title: Taliban Report Release of 291 Afghan Citizens from Pakistani Prisons
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Refugees and Repatriation announced the return of 291 Afghan migrants released from Pakistani prisons. Of these, 264 entered via Torkham and 27 via Spin Boldak. Pakistan has frequently detained and deported Afghans for lacking residency documents or residing illegally.

item.title: Taliban Order Closure of All Private Educational Centers in Nuristan Province
item.description: Local sources report that the Taliban have ordered the closure of all private educational centers in Parun, the capital of Nuristan Province, Afghanistan. The Directorate for the Propagation of Virtue and Prevention of Vice issued letters to these centers, demanding they cease operations and report with their licenses. This action follows previous warnings against expanding English-language education and adds to existing restrictions on girls' education.

item.title: OIC Reaffirms Support for Girls' Education and Aid to Afghanistan
item.description: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting girls' education and providing humanitarian and economic assistance to Afghanistan. At a meeting in Doha, the OIC emphasized counterterrorism, nutrition, and food security as priorities. Cooperation with the UN, World Bank, and EU is deemed essential for coordinating aid efforts amid Afghanistan's ongoing humanitarian and economic challenges.

item.title: Astana prosecutor's office declares journalist's travel ban illegal
item.description: The Astana prosecutor's office has declared the travel ban imposed on journalist Lukpan Akhmedyarov illegal. The ban was previously issued by the capital's police, investigating a case where Akhmedyarov is a witness. His lawyer stated that initiating a criminal case does not justify violating his constitutional rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Extensive Road Repairs to Reduce Accidents by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan will undertake medium repairs on 10,000 kilometers of inter-regional and intra-regional roads between 2025 and 2028. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov announced that measures include reclassifying roads to higher technical categories to separate opposing traffic flows and implementing engineering solutions on high-risk accident sections.

item.title: Polio-Free Afghanistan Urges Universal Vaccination to Prevent Disease Spread
item.description: Polio-Free Afghanistan emphasizes that polio anywhere poses a risk everywhere and urges universal child vaccination. The organization called for all children to be vaccinated, noting ongoing polio circulation in Afghanistan. The UN reported 48 polio cases in Afghanistan and Pakistan this year, with 42 in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Regulate Online Personal Fundraising
item.description: Kazakhstan is proposing new rules to regulate personal online fundraising. Citizens collecting money for personal needs will be required to report on how donations are spent. The Ministry of Culture and Information published the draft project. Violators face administrative or criminal liability. This also includes changes for charitable organizations.
